body.text:
Osmanthus latte: home made osmanthus sauce, with a little sea salt milk cap.
Chestnut basque: the outside is baked a bit burnt, inside still soft.
Hot red wine (no alcohol version): cinnamon, orange skin and clove, suitable for rainy day.
body.background: A small café wants its autumn menu in English for tourists. Short, appetising lines, not a word-for-word list.

why.label: syrup
why.note: The café makes a sweet syrup for this drink. "Sauce" suggests a savoury condiment, such as soy or chilli sauce, which would confuse a reader choosing a sweet latte at the counter.

why.label: foam
why.note: The topping is milk foam with sea salt in it. "Foam" tells the reader it is a soft layer on the drink. "Milk cap" is a mushroom to an English reader, and "sea salt milk" would sound like a salty milk ingredient.

why.label: on top
why.note: Placing the foam on top with "on top" shows where it sits. Writing "with a little sea salt foam" would read as a mixed-in ingredient, not a topping.

out.success: Ah, foam on top, now I get it!

out.ref: Chestnut Basque cheesecake: golden-brown, [caramelised] outside, still soft [and tender] inside.
alts: Chestnut Basque cheesecake: toasty, browned outside, still soft and tender inside.
Chestnut Basque cheesecake: browned and toasty on the outside, soft and tender in the middle.

why.label: golden-brown
why.note: Keeps the writer's colour point but as an adjective describing the cake. "Baked golden-brown" is a sentence about the kitchen; a menu describes what the customer will see.

why.label: caramelised
why.note: A menu term for the browned, slightly sweet crust. It suggests 焦香 without the negative sense of "burnt" or "scorched", which would put readers off.

why.label: still
why.note: The writer's 依然 sets up a contrast: the outside is browned, yet the inside is still soft. Without "still", the sentence just lists two qualities and loses that point.

why.label: tender
why.note: Covers 嫩 as well as 软. "Soft" alone can sound like dry or undercooked; "soft and tender" tells the customer the texture is pleasant.

note.meaning: A soft layer of milk froth sitting on the surface of a drink.
note.usage: Used on café and drink menus to show that a topping sits on the drink, not mixed into it. Better than "with foam", which suggests an ingredient inside the drink.
